newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Benco, Moonstone to auction diamonds.
newsitem.headline: Benco, Moonstone to auction diamonds.

text.p: Benco and Australian-based Moonstone Diamond Corp will on Wednesday auction the first diamonds recovered by their Moonstar diamond mining vessel.
Sidestepping De Beers and the Central Selling Organisation, the companies will auction 2,800 carats recovered during sea trials and the first three weeks of mining.
"Selected South African buyers have been invited to inspect the parcels," Benco chairman John Gurney said in a statement.

"Their offers to purchase are then submitted as sealed tenders and will be opened at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Wednesday," he said, adding that successful buyers will then be notified and, once the transfer of funds has taken place, the new owners will take possession of their diamonds.

Gurney said that this may be regarded as a bold move by what many regard as a minor player in the industry, but he saw no reason why the group should not be able to achieve $200 per carat as forecast at Moonstar's launch late last year.
Moonstone technical director John Bristow said the Moonstar, which was mining concession areas 2(b) near Port Nolloth off South Africa's west coast, had outperformed initial expectations.
"We are most satisfied with progress to date," he said.
